about.what: Hand-judged cross-type More Like This cases: films graded as recommendations for series seeds and series for film seeds, for den-atlas #49 (mixed rows). Same seeds, grades and bases as judged/rail.json, whose `about` defines them; this file only adds titles of the other type. Kept apart because raileval::resolve rejects a judgement whose type differs from the seed's; the #49 scorer change loads both files, keyed by (type, id).
about.shape: `cases` lists seeds in judged/rail.json's order, each with its `seed`, `title` and `split` copied from there. Each `judged` entry is {id, type, title, grade, basis, note?}: `id` is `<type>:<tmdbId>` as in judged/rail.json, and `type` repeats the prefix (`movie` or `series`) so a reader need not parse it. It is always the type the seed is not. A seed with no cross-type candidate is absent.
about.basis: As judged/rail.json. `issue` also covers den-atlas #49, which names the franchise pairs (Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me, the Sex and the City films) as rows a mixed ranker should surface.
about.pooling: Candidates are the cross-type titles in the first ten of #49's recommended mixed arm (per-type pooling, z-mapped cross-type cosines, anchored spread and floors, (type, subgenre) cap) on dataset 5b1c3213b6a1, for each of the 61 seeds. Titles the judge did not know well enough were left unjudged rather than guessed.
